questions.question: What does the "brilliant new colleague" mental model suggest?
options: The model already knows your company's conventions, so keep prompts short
Write prompts as if briefing a capable person who has no background on your task
Always assign the model a senior job title
Ask the model to interview you before every task
questions.explanation: A new colleague is capable but lacks context; if they would need to ask a question, the model probably needs that answer in the prompt.

questions.question: Which block does the line "Under 150 words, plain text, no bullet points" belong to?
questions.explanation: Length, structure and output shape are format instructions.

questions.question: According to the lesson, which building block is most often skipped?
questions.explanation: People usually state the task but forget background, purpose and relevant facts, which help the model make sensible decisions.

questions.question: A drafted reply has the wrong tone for the reader. Which block should you improve first?
questions.explanation: Tone problems usually mean the model did not understand who will read the output; describe the audience more clearly.
